House London #1 · Seat 67

Extend-in-Place

Why aren't we tearing down old buildings?

London planning applications are mostly extensions. Knock-down-and-rebuild is a thin tail. Conditional on filing, approval rates for the two look similar.

Question

Two hypotheses

  • H1: councils refuse demolition-and-rebuild more than extensions.
  • H2: applicants rarely file demolition-and-rebuild in the first place.

Tested on 151,398 Foreman applications sorted by description keywords.

Approval

Change of use

Lower approval than extend

Newham: extend 66% approved vs change of use 26% (largest borough spread). Matches independent PlanIt analysis from House London #0.

HMO converts: ~28% of change-of-use bucket; ~40% approved vs ~48% other converts.

Validation

Checks run

  • 400-app gold sample — classifier macro-F1 0.92
  • 80-row blind re-label — κ 0.883
  • Wilson CIs on approval rates (R)
  • Borough cluster bootstrap on extend vs knock-down gap
  • PLD guest API phrase counts

Keyword sorting on descriptions. Not council ground truth.

Limits

Non-claims

  • Applications filed ≠ homes delivered.
  • No causal model for why owners extend rather than rebuild.
  • Borough rankings exploratory.
